rationales: Smoke consists of solid particles dispersed in air, a gas.
Butter is a colloid, not a solid dispersed in a gas.
Brass is a solid solution of metals.
Fog consists of liquid droplets dispersed in air.
Carbon is in group 14.
Sulphur is in group 16.
Nitrogen is a non-metal in group 15.
Iodine is in group 17.
Dobereiner proposed the law of triads.
Newlands presented the law of octaves.
Moseley established the modern periodic law based on atomic number.
Mendeleev proposed an earlier periodic table and periodic law.
An ionic bond forms through electron transfer and electrostatic attraction.
A covalent bond forms through mutual sharing of electrons.
A metallic bond involves delocalized electrons among metal atoms.
A coordinate bond is a covalent bond in which one atom supplies both shared electrons.
800 °C is close to sodium chloride’s melting point, not its boiling point.
1013 °C is not the accepted boiling point of sodium chloride.
1213 °C is below the accepted boiling point of sodium chloride.
1413 °C is the boiling point given for sodium chloride in the textbook options.
Zinc is solid at room temperature.
Sodium is solid at room temperature.
Hydrogen is a gas at room temperature.
Mercury is liquid at room temperature.
% m/m expresses grams of solute per 100 grams of solution.
% m/v expresses grams of solute per 100 cm³ of solution.
% v/m expresses cm³ of solute per 100 grams of solution.
% v/v expresses cm³ of solute per 100 cm³ of solution.
377 kJ/mol is not sodium’s first ionization energy.
403 kJ/mol is not sodium’s first ionization energy.
419 kJ/mol is not sodium’s first ionization energy.
Sodium’s first ionization energy is approximately 496 kJ/mol.
Thomson proposed the plum pudding model of the atom.
Chadwick discovered the neutron.
Goldstein observed canal rays.
Dalton proposed an early atomic theory.
600 °C is below sodium chloride’s melting point.
750 °C is below sodium chloride’s melting point.
Sodium chloride melts at about 800 °C.
1000 °C is above sodium chloride’s melting point.
Solvent-to-solute is not the usual definition of concentration.
Concentration is expressed as the amount of solute relative to a given amount of solution.
Solvent-to-solution does not express the amount of dissolved substance.
Solute-to-solvent is not the standard ratio defining concentration.
Calcium is heavier than lithium.
Magnesium is heavier than lithium.
Lithium is the lightest metal.
Sodium is heavier than lithium.
H. Moseley established atomic numbers through his work on characteristic X-rays.
Newlands arranged elements by increasing atomic mass and proposed octaves.
Thomson discovered the electron, not atomic number.
Crookes worked on cathode rays and did not discover atomic number.
HCl is polar because its atoms have unequal electronegativities.
NH₃ is polar due to its molecular shape and bond dipoles.
H₂O is polar because its bent shape gives it a net dipole.
H₂ is non-polar because its identical atoms share electrons equally.
Zinc is used to galvanize iron or steel.
Chromium is commonly used for chromium plating, not galvanizing.
Copper is not used to galvanize iron or steel.
Iron is the metal being protected by galvanizing, not the coating metal.
